newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas focus shifts to outer months, prompt slides.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas focus shifts to outer months, prompt slides.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices saw interest switching to the end of the year on Wednesday, traders and brokers said, with the majority of deals done in the third and fourth quarters.
Interest largely disappeared from the day-ahead market, dealers said.
For two days there had been keen buying interest on the day-ahead market at rising prices, with levels reaching 10.70 pence a therm on Tuesday.

But Amoco, which said it had had a problem on a compression platform at Inde 23A, said on Wednesday that that was resolved and the company was meeting all nominations in full at the Bacton beach terminal.
As a result prompt prices eased, and day-ahead gas was talked in the range 10.25/10.50 pence a therm although no deals were heard done and interest was thin.

There was talk of some interest in the year from July, with a bid heard at 12.625 against several offers at 12.70 pence, but no deals were heard done. This interest followed several trades done in the July year on Tuesday at 12.70 pence and marginally above.

Q3 was done several times in a narrow range, with all deals done between 10.30 pence and 10.40 pence a therm. By the close, the quarter was firming slightly with bids heard coming from 10.40 pence and offers around 0.05 pence above this level.
Q4 was also traded several times in a narrow range between 13.30 pence and 13.40 pence, exactly the same level as on Tuesday.
In addition to these, there were also rumours that trade was done more than once in Q1 98 at 15.875 pence, and also at 11.00 pence in Q2, but these were not confirmed.
The IPE futures contract was quiet on Wednesday, with only 120 lots done, most of them in front month May.

The front month had moved up in the morning session, driven by the compression problems at Bacton, a futures broker said, but the month eased slightly in thin afternoon trade as it became clear that the problems were only short-term.

Transco announced that Thursday's temperature is forecast at 8.9 Celsius, down nearly a full degree from the seasonal normal 9.8 Celsius. Consumption is forecast at 213 mcm, or 50 percent of peak day demand.
